chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abi al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abi Imran Amr ibn Mus'ab al-Arzami, from Abi Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

The servant is between three things: calamity, destiny, and blessing. Upon him regarding the calamity from God is patience, which is obligatory; and upon him regarding the destiny from God is submission, which is obligatory; and upon him regarding the blessing from God, the Mighty and Exalted, is gratitude, which is obligatory.
ai.seo_question: What are the three obligatory duties of a believer in response to God's trials, destiny, and blessings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) categorizes the believer's existence into three fundamental states—calamity (bala'), destiny/decree (qada'), and blessings (ni'ma)—each demanding a specific obligatory duty: patience, submission, and gratitude, respectively. This triad reflects the Shia theological emphasis on active spiritual engagement with divine will, where 'qada'' is distinguished from mere fate by requiring conscious acceptance of God's decree. The hadith underscores that these are not optional virtues but fard (obligatory) duties, forming a comprehensive framework for navigating life's fluctuations with spiritual resilience.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-17 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Abil Qasim Abdul Rahman ibn Himad, on the authority of Abi Imran Amr ibn Mus’ab al-Arzami, on the authority of Abi Hamzih al-Somali, “I heard Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) say, ‘

One is caught in between three things: calamities, destiny and blessings. It is incumbent upon him to be patient in the face of calamities sent from God. It is incumbent upon him to submit to the destiny determined for him by God. It is also incumbent upon him to be grateful for the blessings sent to him by the Honorable the Exalted God.”
